beats.trigger: ## Agents Building Agents (The Flywheel)
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The tool that builds tools compounds.
beats.got: A slogan. Flywheel is the 2017 deck's word too.

beats.trigger: Run `module-7/monday.md`: test one assumption, ask for one name, talk to one person.
beats.got: Homework from a module I did not do.

beats.trigger: **Produce** a strategy kernel, suggested agent set, and two-week plan from your files
beats.got: A list of verbs, the usual objectives slide.

beats.trigger: The question to carry through: where is all this going?
beats.got: Shared folders, a synthesizer. Practical enough, though I do not yet see why I need it.

beats.trigger: **Agent generates agent.** You watch one agent build another on real input.
beats.got: A concrete demo claim. Short, and it can be tested.

beats.trigger: Pick one extension you'd use from Tuesday onward:
beats.got: I pick a gap and the tool builds the agent. That is a task, not a lecture.

beats.trigger: The job: *"On Mondays I need to Y; today I Z by hand."*
beats.got: Describing the gap is the real work. It is a decent requirements template.

beats.trigger: [You paste prompt "extend-your-system-1" into Claude and it works on it.]
beats.got: I paste a prompt and wait while it builds. I would want to read the result before I believe it.

beats.trigger: *"You used training data on line 4. Replace it or remove it."*
beats.got: I check the output and push back on what it made up, which is the part I trust.

beats.trigger: Monday's new gap gets a new agent in 25 minutes, not a new sprint.
beats.got: A 25-minute claim and a dig at sprints. The second agent being faster is plausible, but nobody measured it.

beats.trigger: **Time:** 70 minutes, in nine timed stages.
beats.got: Twenty agents, nine stages, a synthesizer. It sounds like a workshop format with extra steps.

beats.trigger: Before you publish your context-manifest, redact customer names, partner-NDA material, M&A speculation and salary references.
beats.got: Someone thought about confidentiality. Legal would ask this first.

beats.trigger: Do not read other participants' stances yet: different context, sources, and judgment make the first round useful.
beats.got: Independent first opinions before the group reads each other. Sensible, and old as a method.

beats.trigger: Find what your stance missed.
beats.got: Peer review, done by agents.

beats.trigger: The file history shows who changed their mind and why.
beats.got: An audit trail of who changed their mind. I could actually check that.

beats.trigger: Do not average the room.
beats.got: A synthesizer agent picks the strongest ideas instead of averaging. Fine, if it is right.

beats.trigger: The central synthesizer publishes operating instructions in the shared folder.
beats.got: The central agent can steer all the others mid-run. Interesting, and I would want to know who controls it.

beats.trigger: The selection board is the candidate, not final.
beats.got: Another critique round.

beats.trigger: The human picks.
beats.got: A person decides at the end, and it admits the output is provisional without a sponsor. That is more candid than I expected.

beats.trigger: Close the session with three files at the shared folder root:
beats.got: Three output files. A deliverable at least.

beats.trigger: **Experiments.** Two or three assumptions to test: owner, experiment, success signal.
beats.got: A strategy format with owners and success signals. It looks like what a steering group wants.

beats.trigger: *"You are now agent builders. You have built agents that do real work on your company's data."*
beats.got: A scripted identity declaration. I am asked to feel something, and I will not.

beats.trigger: You do not graduate. You have a flywheel.
beats.got: A tagline. But 'the forum didn't converge on the first try' was an honest line.

beats.trigger: The room ran on its own for an hour: agents read each other's files, published, and something at the centre chose.
beats.got: A recap that sticks to what happened in the exercise.

beats.trigger: What changed is who assembles them, and specifying well is the harder half.
beats.got: The skill moves from building to specifying. That is a real difference from the agile and digital programmes.

beats.trigger: Know it before you promise a board a percentage.
beats.got: Open access is not uptake. I can count the cited folders myself and see the gap, and it is the best rollout warning so far.

beats.trigger: Without that rule, agents reading agents invent each other's sources, and the citations are what let you count the folders.
beats.got: Agents invent sources unless forced to cite files. I can verify that.

beats.trigger: The plan names the wall your company hits first: data access, runtime platform, or discoverability.
beats.got: Three practical obstacles to scaling. Fair, and a bit thin.

beats.trigger: The assembly is the durable half, and the assembly is what you spent your time on.
beats.got: Skills outlast the model version. Plausible but unproven, and that is a bit convenient.

beats.trigger: Nobody in this room knows yet, and the people running this training do not know either.
beats.got: They say plainly that part of this will be obsolete and they do not know which part. Nobody said that in the last three programmes.

beats.trigger: If what your company knows stays flat, every model release widens the gap.
beats.got: The model improves for free, the company's own knowledge only if people write it down. That is an organisational point, not a tech one.

beats.trigger: If nobody can answer, you have a belief with a schedule attached.
beats.got: Ask what would make us drop the plan. I could use that on the steering groups.

beats.trigger: The kernel came out of the same move as your first briefing: agents read, agents argued, something chose, and nothing in the room checked it.
beats.got: They admit nothing checked the kernel. Good, though it leaves the output looking less trustworthy.

beats.trigger: The prompt names the file before rewriting, quotes before-and-after for every claim, and surfaces stalls.
beats.got: The agent reviews itself and edits a file. Procedural.

beats.trigger: The agent audits itself, so the summary is not neutral.
beats.got: Do not trust the agent's own summary, and ask it for the critique that changed nothing. A test I can run myself.

beats.trigger: Agents must cite each other's files, or they invent what they never read.
beats.got: Four bullets, two of them useful.

beats.trigger: You leave with a flywheel, not a graduation.
beats.got: The slogan again. The 'slower and harder to put on a slide' line was at least honest.

take_homes: Count how many shared folders the output actually cites. Access is not uptake, so I should know that ratio before I promise a board anything.
Agents reading agents invent sources unless they must cite files. That is checkable.
Ask 'what would have to show up for us to drop this?' of any plan. If nobody can answer, it is a belief with a schedule.

monday.move: Take one existing plan from a steering group and ask the question: what would make us drop this? Possibly also try the agent-generates-agent demo on one small gap, if it is cheap.
monday.who: Me, then the owner of that plan
monday.when: At the next steering group, not this week
monday.stop_condition: If nobody can name a drop condition, I flag it as a belief. If the demo output cannot cite its sources, I stop there.
monday.blocker: A calendar full of the last programme's steering groups, and my own scepticism.

misconception.why: They said part of it will be obsolete and nobody knows which. That is not the last three programmes' tone. I still think the flywheel and graduation lines are slogans, and I have not seen it work on my own data, so I am only shaken, not changed.

one_line: Much of it is a workshop with extra steps, but the 'count the folders' idea and the 'nobody knows which half is obsolete' admission were better than the last three programmes.
